title: "Resources: Document control and records"
order: 22
---

Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[21 CFR 606.100 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  — the SOP (standard operating procedure) regulation behind this module's "available… where the
  procedures are performed" citation. Local verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/606.100.md`.

- **[21 CFR 606.160 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.160)**
  — the records regulation, source of this module's Good Documentation Practice citation
  (paragraph (a)(1)) and the product-record retention clause (paragraph (d)), already taught in
  full in `reading-a-cfr-citation`. Local verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/606.160.md`.

- **[21 CFR 606.120 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.120)**
  — the labeling-controls regulation, source of the "stocks of obsolete labels shall be
  destroyed" clause this module reads as Part 606's own closest parallel to obsolete-document
  removal. Local verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/606.120.md`.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations collection](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)**
  — the U.S. Government Publishing Office's official CFR collection. Use it as a fallback primary
  source if eCFR or Cornell is ever unreachable, or to pull an official PDF of a full CFR part for
  the record.

- **[What Is The Difference In Controlled & Uncontrolled Documents?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=viRq4F_6LnU)**
  (InstantGMP , Inc., from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. InstantGMP is
  a GMP (good manufacturing practice) software and compliance company; this video walks the
  controlled-versus-uncontrolled-document distinction in general GMP terms, not blood-specifically
  and without any AABB or 606.100(b) language — use it for the mechanics of the distinction itself,
  then map it onto Brookfield's binder. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP
  200).

- **[Atlassian: 4 ways knowledge management assists your IT service
  practice](https://www.atlassian.com/itsm/knowledge-management/ITIL)** — a practical explainer on
  ITIL's knowledge management practice, the ITSM (IT service management) practice this module
  bridges document control to. Use it to see knowledge management argued in full on its own ITIL
  terms, then re-read this module's point that document control adds a requirement a knowledge base
  usually doesn't: the current version has to be the *only* version physically present at the point
  of use, not just the newest one findable centrally. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[Red Hat: What is a configuration management database
  (CMDB)?](https://www.redhat.com/en/topics/automation/what-is-a-configuration-management-database-cmdb)**
  — a vendor-neutral-enough explainer on CMDBs and configuration items (CIs), backing this module's
  one-paragraph bridge that a controlled document is itself a versioned CI with a defined baseline,
  and Quality's master document list is functionally Lakeshore's CMDB for procedures. Use it to see
  the CI/CMDB concept argued in full IT terms before applying it to a paper binder at a satellite
  site. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Pharmaguideline: Requirements for Good Documentation Practice
  (GDP)](https://www.pharmaguideline.com/2014/07/requirements-for-good-documentation-practice-gdp.html)**
  — an industry explainer on Good Documentation Practice generally (contemporaneous entries,
  legible and indelible records, dated signatures, no backdating, a proper single-line-strikeout
  correction method) — the same discipline this module's 606.160(a)(1) citation demands of a
  document-control record like a site lead's acknowledgment, argued in the fuller, general-GMP form
  that 606.160(a)(1) itself doesn't spell out step by step. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
